title: calling black men, especially younger black men, back toward discipline, purpose, education, mentorship + thinking beyond the immediate moment.

body.text: black men .. we gotta step up.
there really isn’t a softer way for me to say it.
we need more skills. more education. more discipline. more purpose. more thought behind the decisions we’re making.
because no matter how much work u put into yourself, one decision made without thinking can interrupt years of progress.
and i’m not speaking like somebody who always got it right.
as a black man, i’ve made decisions that disappointed people who genuinely cared about me.
and that taught me something.
our decisions don’t only belong to us.
when u have people who love u, support u, believe in u + want to see u make it home .. what u do with your life can affect their lives too.
that doesn’t mean live your life for everybody else.
it means understand that your actions have weight.
think beyond today.
think about tomorrow.
think about your family.
think about the people who still want u here.
think about the opportunities that disappear when one emotional or irrational decision changes everything.
i feel like we need that reminder right now.
especially for young black men who are constantly being shown examples of what destruction looks like, but not enough examples of what direction, discipline + purpose can look like.
and this is part of why i built innerg intel.
my name is nas. i’m the founder of innerg intel, and part of this mission is raising the frequency around conversations that keep getting drowned out.
purpose.
discipline.
ownership.
education.
technology.
leadership.
self-awareness.
the things that can actually help somebody build a life instead of only reacting to one.
i also think we need to repair the relationship between generations of men.
why aren’t more older men intentionally reaching back to guide younger men?
and at the same time, why aren’t more younger men seeking wisdom from men who already survived situations they’re just beginning to experience?
we need mentors.
we need mentees.
we need spaces where men can tell each other the truth without every conversation becoming judgment, competition or ego.
there’s a lot happening right now involving black men. rappers. court cases. violence. death. street politics. everybody has something to say about what happened, who did what + who should be free.
but at some point, i think we have to ask:
what are these conversations actually doing for the black men who are still alive?
because knowing every detail about somebody else’s destruction does not automatically help us avoid our own.
if u want to talk about the gangs, wars + street politics all day, there are already spaces dedicated to that.
i want to create more space for the brothers trying to stay alive.
the ones trying to learn.
the ones trying to become better fathers, sons, partners, friends, builders + men.
the ones who know they need direction but may not know where to find it yet.
if that message connects with u, share it.
and if u know other black men already doing this work, tag them too.
i’m not interested in pretending i’m the only person speaking about it.
i want the frequency louder.
more mentors.
more teachers.
more builders.
more men willing to tell another brother:
think before u throw your future away.
innerg intel is on the road to 1,000 youtube subscribers.
but more important than the number is what we’re building around it.
if the message makes sense to u, support it. share it. add your perspective.
and keep reminding the brothers around u that purpose still matters.
